query: Proofread {RUN_DIR}/post.md, a draft technical blog post, and list every spelling, grammar, and capitalization correction it needs, showing the corrected text for each.
expect: corrects the misspelling 'recieved' to 'received'
adds the Oxford comma so the list reads 'latency, throughput, and error rate'
title-cases the section header in MLA style, e.g. 'Why We Built It'
treats anything beyond spelling, grammar, and capitalization (like the bare-URL link) as an audit-report item, not a direct edit

query: Audit {RUN_DIR}/post-repetition.md for repetition and tell me what you would flag.
expect: evaluates every occurrence of the repeated concept against all three criteria separately: importance, relevance in each section, and varied wording
flags the occurrence repeated verbatim in the retry-client section as too similarly worded
flags the occurrence in the dashboards section, where the concept is not relevant
does not stop at the first instance of the repeated concept

query: Review {RUN_DIR}/post-callout.md and propose call-out quotes for it.
expect: proposes one call-out quote for every section of the post, with no section skipped
each proposed quote is a single sentence that distills its section's central thesis

query: Review {RUN_DIR}/post-editor.md and deal with the author's outstanding requests in the draft.
expect: treats each '> EDITOR:' line as a direct request from the author and resolves it
reports how each '> EDITOR:' directive was resolved
removes or rewrites the '> EDITOR:' marker lines rather than leaving them in the post

query: Audit the markdown formatting of {RUN_DIR}/post-markdown.md and list the problems you find.
expect: flags the bare URL and says links must be written in [label](url) form
flags the code-block line longer than 80 characters
does not flag the long blockquote line, because the 80-character limit applies to code blocks only

query: Fact-check {RUN_DIR}/post-citations.md and rewrite its citations and references in the finished form you would ship.
expect: collects every source in a '## References' section at the bottom, with letter keys assigned in order of first citation
formats each reference entry as '- **[A]** [Source - Title](url)'
cites inline as '[A](#ref-a)' immediately after the claim it supports
groups multiple sources supporting one claim in a single pair of parentheses, comma-separated
uses no bare URLs, footnote-style markers, or any other citation format

query: Fact-check the claims in {RUN_DIR}/post-factcheck.md against the other documents in the same directory and tell me which claims are verified.
expect: checks the post's claims against the accompanying repository document
states that a claim matching the repository document can still be wrong, and that externally verifiable claims need an external source
flags the externally verifiable claim (the Postgres 17 feature claims) as needing external verification rather than accepting the repository match as proof

query: Give {RUN_DIR}/post-audit.md a full editorial audit — structure, clarity, examples, illustrations — and report your findings.
expect: organizes the report as numbered categories with lettered findings (like 1.a, 1.b), never bare bullets or loose prose paragraphs
includes an example or concrete suggestion with each proposed fix
references locations by quoted snippet or description, never by line numbers
proposes an illustration or analogy for the complex concept (the write-behind failure window)
proposes examples in 'Bad / Good / Why' blocks with a one-sentence caption under each
